title: Slider Frame
description: The wrapper for a carousel, supplying the arrow and dot presentation the live site uses on its homepage and single-page sliders. The nav itself is drawn by whichever carousel is inside — Slick under Tour Operator, Swiper under the Carousel Block — so neither set of markup is ours to put in a block-style JSON. It applies to core/group and to the two query blocks Tour Operator's "Enable Slider" checkbox extends (core/query, core/terms-query), because Slick appends its arrows and dots to the *parent* of the template element — custom.js:479-480 — which is the query block itself. This style declares the colour and geometry values as custom properties on that element and assets/styles/core-group.css binds them to both vendors' hooks, which is the pattern in wp-thirdparty-markup-styling: scope to the is-style class so natural specificity wins without !important. Live measured 2026-08-20 (arrows #B4A48C fully round, dots #938673 fully round) is superseded at Zared's direction 2026-09-03: the arrows are a heavier chevron in primary-500 with a brand-600 hover, and the dots are a lighter, thinner square-cornered bar. The vendor glyph fonts are switched off and the chevron is Phosphor's caret-left/caret-right (256x256, filled path) - the same icon set the section's rating-stars mask uses - inlined in core-group.css as a mask so the colour still resolves through these tokens. The glyph's viewBox is square, so --sd-slider-chevron-size sets both box dimensions with no aspect calc needed. --sd-slider-slide-gutter restates Tour Operator's own 15px slide inset as a number a shelf can change: core-group.css binds it to the vendor's .slick-slide rule, and the sd-slider-tight modifier sets it to 0 for a shelf whose design is one continuous band rather than a row of cards.
